digest.top_line: PEACE V-STORM: 4-yr MFS 76% vs 63% with elective nodal RT vs MDT, HR 0·62, and DBCG IMN2 puts 15y OS 65.0% vs 60.8% behind internal mammary nodal irradiation.
digest.tldr: Two nodal-coverage trials, same lesson: treating the at-risk nodal basin rather than the visible lesion buys durable control. Prostate leads (PEACE V-STORM cuts pelvic relapse 29%→8%, ADT-free survival 77% vs 60%, no added G2+ GI/GU), breast follows (IMN2 extends the OS gain to 1-3 positive nodes, HR 0.85). Lymphoma is dose de-escalation, not coverage.

sites.intro: Expert opinion, not evidence: 8-12 Gy is the working standard for indolent cutaneous lymphoma, and the 4 Gy question stays contested.

studies.name: EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Tumour Group RT Recommendations
studies.tldr: EORTC expert opinion consolidates reduced-dose RT (4-12 Gy) as standard for indolent cutaneous lymphomas, with a dose algorithm across subtypes.
details: 🧭 Expert-opinion recommendations, not a systematic review; no randomised trials support radiation-based therapy selection over other modalities (per the paper)

details.text: 📐 MF plaques/tumours: usual dose 8-12 Gy in two or three fractions, with 1-year local control ≥ 92 % reported after low-dose RT
⚠️ 4 Gy (one or two fractions) gave an inferior local control rate in MF, so the paper does not treat 4 Gy as interchangeable with 8-12 Gy
📐 Low-dose TSEBT 8-12 Gy for palliation in advanced disease; up to 24 Gy to induce remission before autologous stem cell transplant

details: 📐 pcALCL: RT effective with few relapses at doses of 20 Gy; palliative 2×4 Gy for prompt symptom relief
📐 CD4+ small/medium-sized T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder: 4 Gy in two fractions, 100 % remission and no local relapses in the cited series
📐 pcMZL/pcFCL: 4 Gy can be curative in many cases; lesions > 5 cm treated with 4 Gy had worse outcomes
⚠️ Ultra-low-dose 4 Gy is contested in pcMZL/pcFCL: the ILROG register series (n=440) reported local relapse 28 % vs 5 % (p < 0.001) against 8-50 Gy

details.text: 🔗 Response-adapted escalation to a cumulative 24 Gy is proposed for residual disease or local failure after 4 Gy
📐 DLBCL leg type: consolidation after systemic therapy may be reduced to 30 Gy; 20 Gy consolidation reported with relatively lower toxicity

details: ⚠️ Tables 1 and 2 arrived with uncertain row/value association in the source extraction, so per-series dose-to-outcome pairings beyond those stated in the body text are not attributed here
studies.significance: The actionable content is the dose ladder, not a result: 8-12 Gy in 2-3 fractions for MF lesions, 4 Gy in 2 fractions for CD4+ SMPLPD, 20 Gy for pcALCL, and a response-adapted climb to 24 Gy when 4 Gy fails in pcMZL/pcFCL. The 4 Gy-vs-higher-dose relapse gap (28 % vs 5 %) is the number that should gate ultra-low-dose use outside palliation.
studies.monday_clinic: In indolent cutaneous lymphoma treated with skin-directed RT, this supports reduced-dose regimens with a response-adapted escalation path when 4 Gy fails; it does not extend to advanced MF, Sézary syndrome, or DLBCL leg type, where the authors say combined-modality gaps remain.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Expert opinion** from the EORTC cutaneous lymphoma tumour group, synthesising mostly **retrospective** series plus a handful of small prospective cohorts into dose recommendations (Figs 2A/2B). Not a systematic review, no pooled estimate.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: MF plaques and tumours: **8-12 Gy in two or three fractions**, 1-year local control **≥ 92 %**, with 4 Gy in one or two fractions **inferior** for local control. Low-dose TSEBT **8-12 Gy** palliates advanced skin disease; **up to 24 Gy** pre-autologous transplant. pcALCL controlled at **20 Gy** with 2×4 Gy for palliation; CD4+ SMPLPD at **4 Gy in two fractions**; pcMZL/pcFCL often cured by **4 Gy**, escalating to a cumulative **24 Gy** for residual or recurrent disease.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The recurring signal across cited series is that ultra-low dose buys convenience at some cost in durability: the ILROG register (n=440) reported **local relapse 28 % vs 5 % (p < 0.001)** for 4 Gy in 2 fractions vs 8-50 Gy, while other retrospective comparisons found RT dose non-significant. The paper does not reconcile these.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents localised or oligolesional indolent cutaneous lymphoma (MF, pcALCL, CD4+ SMPLPD, pcMZL, pcFCL) where skin-directed RT is being chosen. Does not represent advanced MF, Sézary syndrome, or aggressive CTCL variants (panniculitis-like, gamma/delta, CD8+ epidermotropic, NK/T), where the authors state low-dose RT has a limited role.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The dose thresholds rest on single-institution retrospectives with heterogeneous endpoints (ORR, CR, local relapse, TTNT), no common follow-up, and no comparator arm, so the 4 Gy-versus-higher-dose question stays unsettled between series. The authors themselves call for a prospective randomised trial with translational correlates.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Two ongoing combination trials are named: low-dose TSEBT with **mogamulizumab** (NCT04128072, phase 2) and with **brentuximab** (NCT02822586, phase 1), plus low-dose TSEBT 12 Gy ± mechlorethamine gel maintenance. An **ESTRO consensus guideline** is anticipated and will carry the shared-decision-making framing this paper defers to.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This is a dose-prescription document: 8-12 Gy in 2-3 fractions for MF lesions, 20 Gy for pcALCL, 4 Gy in 2 fractions for CD4+ SMPLPD, and a response-adapted climb to a cumulative 24 Gy after a failed 4 Gy in pcMZL/pcFCL. The 28 % vs 5 % relapse gap (p < 0.001) in the 440-patient ILROG register is the argument against treating 4 Gy as a default outside palliation.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: RT is positioned as a low-toxicity partner to systemic therapy rather than a competitor: consolidation after systemic treatment in DLBCL leg type can drop to 30 Gy, or 20 Gy with lower toxicity, and TSEBT is framed as a bridge before autologous transplant at up to 24 Gy. Two combination trials with mogamulizumab (NCT04128072) and brentuximab (NCT02822586) are the sequencing questions in play.

sites.intro: IMNI's OS benefit holds on modern systemic therapy and extends into the 1-3 node subgroup most guidelines still exclude, from a laterality-allocated cohort with real contamination in both directions.

studies.name: DBCG IMN2
studies.tldr: 15y OS 65.0% vs 60.8% with IMNI, adjusted HR 0.85 (0.76-0.94), p=0.0016, in 4541 node-positive pts on modern systemic therapy.
details: 🔍 Nationwide prospective cohort, N=4541, 2007-14, six RT centres; IMNI allocated by LATERALITY (right yes, left no), ITT by side, median f/u 13.7y
📐 RT: 48Gy/24Fx (26.2%) or 50Gy/25Fx (73.2%), 3D conformal wide tangents in free-breathing; IMN target intercostal space 1-4; axilla II-III + level IV all pts
🔗 IMNI effect held in 1-3 positive nodes (n=3100): HR 0.85 (0.73-0.97), the exact subgroup most guidelines currently exclude
⚠️ ER-/HER2+ subgroup ran the other way: HR 1.49 (0.98-2.25), interaction p=0.021, explorative and unadjusted for multiplicity
⚠️ Contamination both directions: IMNI reported in 10.1% of left-sided pts (n=238) and 344 right-sided pts treated without it, biasing the ITT estimate toward null
⚠️ Dose separation imperfect: median IMN CTV V90% 94.6% (IQR 64.8-100.0) right vs 20.4% (IQR 0.9-55.8) left, so left-sided pts got real incidental dose
🔗 vs KROG 08-06 (n=735), the only other 3D-based IMNI study: OS HR 0.87 (0.57-1.31), ns but underpowered; vs EBCTCG regional nodal RT rate ratio 0.90 (0.84-0.96)

details.text: 📊 Cardiac + lung safety at 15 years, right-sided (IMNI) vs left-sided (no IMNI)
📊 OS by nodal burden and tumour location (Fig 3/4, adjusted HRs)

details: ⚠️ Location signal inverted vs prior teaching: lateral tumours HR 0.81 (0.71-0.93) vs medial/central 0.89 (0.76-1.05), opposite of the EBCTCG/IMN1 expectation (interaction p=0.37)
📐 Premenopausal HR 0.64 (0.50-0.82) vs postmenopausal 0.90 (0.80-1.01), interaction p=0.014; age 35-49 HR 0.57 (0.43-0.77)

verdict.rationale: Prospective nationwide cohort, laterality-allocated (not randomised), 13.7y f/u, primary OS endpoint met; directly contradicts guidelines omitting IMNI at 1-3 nodes.
verdict.audience: Macrometastatic node-positive breast cancer, adjuvant loco-regional RT, no…

studies.significance: The 1-3 node subgroup is the whole point: HR 0.85 (0.73-0.97) in 3100 pts, the population several guidelines exclude from IMNI. Delivered with plain 3D wide tangents, 48-50Gy, free-breathing, so the benefit does not require gating or protons. Cardiac death 0.2% vs 0.7% at 15y argues the historic trade-off has largely dissolved.
studies.monday_clinic: In a right- or left-sided node-positive pt with 1-3 macrometastases finishing taxane-based adjuvant chemo, this supports including the internal mammary chain rather than omitting it on nodal burden alone; it does not extend to pts treated with neoadjuvant systemic therapy, who were excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Nationwide **population-based prospective cohort** in six Danish RT centres, 2007-14, allocating IMNI by **tumour laterality** (right-sided yes, left-sided no) under national guideline, analysed by intention-to-treat on side. Registered NCT06549920. Median follow-up **13.7 years** for OS, 13.2 years for distant metastasis, end of follow-up November 2023.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **4541 of 5206** assessed pts with **macrometastatic node-positive** breast cancer receiving loco-regional RT; 2194 right-sided, 2347 left-sided. Median age 59, **68.3% had 1-3 positive nodes**, 84.8% ER+, 17.5% HER2+, 46.5% mastectomy. Excluded: prior malignancy, bilateral disease, **neoadjuvant systemic therapy** (n=359), recurrence before RT, non-standard RT.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Chemotherapy was three cycles EC (epirubicin 900 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2) then three cycles docetaxel 100 mg/m2; **96.2% of chemo-treated pts got a taxane**. Tamoxifen premenopausal, **aromatase inhibitor postmenopausal**; trastuzumab concomitant with chemo and RT in HER2+ (13.5% overall).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **48 Gy/24 Fx before 2009, 50 Gy/25 Fx after** (26.2% and 73.2% of pts), **3D conformal wide tangents in free-breathing**, no gating. IMN target was **intercostal space 1-4**; all pts also had axilla level II-III, interpectoral and level IV, with level I only for ≥6 positive nodes or <10 nodes removed. QA in 2837 plans: median IMN CTV **V90% 94.6% right vs 20.4% left**.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary OS endpoint met. Secondary endpoints and subgroups are tabulated above; **no subgroup permitted safe omission of IMNI**, including the post hoc 1-3 node analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Death from ischaemic or valvular heart disease at 15y was **0.2% right-sided vs 0.7% left-sided**, and secondary lung cancer death 1.8% vs 2.2%, both numerically favouring the irradiated side. Left-sided **median mean heart dose 2.3 Gy (IQR 1.6-3.7)**, comparable to 2.1 Gy achieved with respiratory gating in 2015-21. Smoking status, cardiac comorbidity and non-fatal cardiac events were not captured.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: OS point estimates converge across the three modern datasets: **0.85 here, 0.90 EBCTCG** rate ratio for regional nodal RT, **0.87 in KROG 08-06** (n=735, ns, underpowered against an anticipated 10% absolute gain). The 4.2% absolute 15y gain also matches DBCG IMN1's 4.7%, so a more effective systemic backbone did not erode the RT effect.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents macrometastatic node-positive breast cancer treated with upfront surgery, taxane-based chemotherapy, AI or tamoxifen, trastuzumab where indicated, and 3D-based loco-regional RT. Does not represent pts receiving neoadjuvant systemic therapy (explicitly excluded), and IMNI efficacy in left-sided disease is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Allocation by laterality means the **IMNI arm is also the right-sided arm**: any laterality-linked confounder (cardiac dose, incidental lung dose, contralateral anatomy) is inseparable from the treatment effect, and left-sided pts served as controls for an intervention they could not receive. **238 left-sided pts (10.1%) got IMNI anyway** and 344 right-sided pts did not, diluting toward null. Subgroup and IHC-subtype analyses were explorative with **no correction for multiple testing**, so the ER-/HER2+ reversal (p=0.021) is fragile.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The reader's real question is whether IMNI survives modern systemic therapy, and the answer here is that the absolute gain (4.2% at 15y) is unchanged from the pre-taxane IMN1 era (4.7%). Because right-sided pts with imperfect coverage (lower quartile <64.8% V90%) sat in the IMNI arm and 25% of left-sided pts exceeded 55.8% coverage, the true effect of a fully covered IMN volume is plausibly larger than 0.85.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The 1-3 node subgroup carries HR 0.85 (0.73-0.97) in 3100 pts, the exact group guidelines exclude from IMNI, and it was delivered with 48-50Gy 3D wide tangents in free-breathing to intercostal space 1-4, no gating or protons required. Cardiac death 0.2% vs 0.7% at 15y removes the usual counterweight.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: A taxane, trastuzumab and AI backbone did not cancel the RT effect: the 4.2% absolute 15y OS gain matches the pre-taxane IMN1 era (4.7%). Systemic escalation therefore does not substitute for nodal coverage, though pts on ADCs and immunotherapy were not represented.

open_questions: Does IMNI benefit persist with ADCs and adjuvant immunotherapy
Can IMNI be omitted after neoadjuvant therapy with nodal pCR
Is ER-/HER2+ a genuine predictor of IMNI harm

sites.intro: The nodal-coverage question in oligorecurrent disease gets its first randomised read: pelvic ENRT beats metastasis-directed SBRT on every control endpoint, though at α=0·20 the MFS primary is not significant by conventional standards.

studies.name: PEACE V-STORM
studies.tldr: 4-yr MFS 76% vs 63% with elective nodal RT vs MDT, HR 0.62 (80% CI 0.44-0.86), p=0.063.
details: 🔍 Phase 2 open-label RCT, 21 hospitals in 6 countries, 196 randomised, 190 evaluable (MDT 97, ENRT 93)
📐 α set at 0·20 two-sided, 80% power, so 80% CIs are reported and p≤0·20 counts as significant for the 1° endpoint

subdetails: MDT: SBRT 30 Gy/3 fx every other day, 90% of PTV, 3 mm margin, IMRT/VMAT with daily IGRT
MDT alternative: bilateral extended sLND of the true pelvis (12 pts total chose surgery)
ENRT: 45 Gy/25 fx whole pelvis with SIB 65 Gy to PET-positive nodes; 45 Gy/25 fx alone post-sLND
Pelvic CTV per modified RTOG 2009 template, upper limit L4-L5 interspace
Both arms: 6 months of ADT; prostate bed 66 Gy/33 fx advised for pT3-4, Gleason ≥8, or positive margin

details.text: 📊 Site of relapse, MDT (n=97) vs ENRT (n=93)

details: 🔍 Benefit is a pattern-of-failure story: M1a nodal spread 28% MDT vs 14% ENRT, bone and lung near-identical
📐 Prespecified subgroups (MDT type, tracer) plus post-hoc ones; PSA <1 favoured ENRT HR 0·27 (0·14-0·52) vs ≥1 HR 1·00 (0·67-1·50), interaction p=0·029
📐 PSMA-staged pts HR 0·48 (0·32-0·72) vs choline HR 1·21 (0·64-2·28), interaction p=0·12
⚠️ Adding the pelvic field did not raise GI toxicity: 4-yr G2+ GI 7% MDT vs 9% ENRT (absolute difference 2%, p=0·93)
⚠️ GU also flat between arms: 4-yr G2+ GU 28% MDT vs 31% ENRT (absolute difference 3%, p=0·73)
⚠️ The toxicity driver was the prostate bed, not the pelvis: bed inclusion gave OR 4·6 (95% CI 1·5-15·8, p=0·0085) for G2+ GI and OR 1·85 (0·95-3·60, p=0·068) for G2+ GU, both post hoc
⚠️ Sceptic's read: p=0·063 only clears the bar because α was set at 0·20; at conventional α this MFS result is not significant
⚠️ Open-label with investigator-attributed AEs and no central PET review at baseline or follow-up
⚠️ OS, cancer-specific survival and time to castration resistance had too few events (11 deaths, 1 prostate cancer-related) to report
🔗 vs GETUG-P07-OLIGOPELVIS (single-arm ENRT): 3-yr bRFS 45% there vs 57% at 4 yr here, but that trial used choline and a higher median PSA (3-4 ng/mL)
🔗 vs RADIOSA / EXTEND: ADT-free interval >48 mo (median not reached with ENRT) vs 33 mo and >24 mo respectively

verdict.rationale: Randomised, prespecified primary endpoint, adequate follow-up, but phase 2 powered at α=0·20; every secondary endpoint moves the same direction. Awaits POINTER-PC phase 3.
verdict.audience: PET-detected pelvic nodal oligorecurrence (≤5 nodes), post-RP or post-RT, no M1

studies.significance: Locoregional RFS is the RT read: 85% vs 62% at 4 yr, HR 0·45 (80% CI 0·31-0·65), and pelvic nodal relapse fell from 29% to 8%, so the elective field converts nodal salvage into durable regional control. 45 Gy/25 fx with a 65 Gy SIB added no GI toxicity over SBRT alone; the prostate bed, not the pelvis, drove G2+ GI (OR 4·6).
studies.monday_clinic: In a man with PSMA-detected pelvic nodal oligorecurrence and PSA below 1 ng/mL, this supports elective pelvic nodal coverage with a nodal boost over node-only MDT alongside 6 months of ADT; the benefit was absent at PSA ≥1 (HR 1·00) and the trial excludes bone, visceral, or above-bifurcation disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Phase 2, open-label, investigator-initiated RCT**, 1:1 by minimisation, 21 hospitals across Australia, Belgium, Italy, Norway, Spain and Switzerland. Stratified by PET tracer (choline vs PSMA) and MDT type (sLND vs SBRT/SIB). Recruited June 2018 to April 2021; median follow-up **50 months** (IQR 42-58).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Biochemical relapse after radical local treatment with **up to five PET-detected pelvic nodal oligorecurrences** (pelvis defined to the aortic bifurcation, common iliac included); WHO PS 0-1. Bone, visceral, and above-bifurcation nodes excluded, as was testosterone <50 ng/dL. Median PSA at inclusion 1·00 vs 0·85 ng/mL; **81-83% staged with PSMA PET**; 91% vs 86% EAU high-risk BCR.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Both groups received **6 months of LHRH agonist or antagonist**, started no later than the first fraction (or day 1-10 post-sLND). All patients who started ADT completed it.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: MDT arm: **SBRT 30 Gy in 3 fractions** every other day to 90% of the PTV, 3 mm margin, IMRT/VMAT with daily IGRT, or bilateral extended sLND. ENRT arm: **45 Gy in 25 fractions to the whole pelvis with a 65 Gy simultaneous integrated boost** to PET-positive nodes, modified RTOG 2009 template to the L4-L5 interspace, IMRT/rotational mandatory with benchmark-case QA. Prostate bed (≥66 Gy/33 fx) advised for high-risk features and delivered in **25% of MDT vs 41% of ENRT** patients.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: metastasis-free survival** (any M1 on PET, or death); a local or pelvic nodal recurrence did NOT count as an event. Secondary: biochemical RFS, locoregional RFS, ADT-free survival, and cumulative CTCAE grade 2 or worse GU/GI events to 48 months. OS, cancer-specific survival and time to castration resistance were prespecified but had too few events.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **No treatment-related deaths.** Most common grade 3 events were urinary incontinence (6% MDT vs 10% ENRT) and diarrhoea (1% vs 2%). Serious RT-related events in 1 MDT and 2 ENRT patients, including one **recto-urethral fistula requiring surgery** in the ENRT group; four serious events followed sLND.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: ENRT here reached **57% 4-yr biochemical RFS** against **45% at 3 yr in single-arm GETUG-P07-OLIGOPELVIS**, though that trial used choline and enrolled at median PSA 3-4 ng/mL. Time off ADT exceeded **48 months** (median not reached with ENRT) versus 33 months in RADIOSA and more than 24 months in EXTEND.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents men with choline or PSMA PET-detected pelvic nodal oligorecurrence, up to five nodes below the aortic bifurcation, fit for 6 months of ADT. Does not represent bone, visceral, or para-aortic disease, unresectable local relapse, or patients whose previous fields overlap the intended pelvis.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: MFS counted only M1 events, so the pelvic-node relapses ENRT prevents are excluded from the primary endpoint and reappear only in the locoregional secondary. No central PET review at baseline or follow-up, and curves did not separate in year one during ADT, so the proportional-hazards read leans on the post-testosterone-recovery period.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The predominant relapse after MDT was locoregional, which the authors read as PSMA PET sensitivity being **insufficient for a one-time node-only approach in at least half of patients**. Repeat salvage remained feasible: 28 MDT patients received a further course of MDT at recurrence. POINTER-PC and GETUG-P12-OLIGOPELVIS 2 are the confirmatory phase 3 trials.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The field-size decision is the whole trial: 45 Gy/25 fx to a modified RTOG pelvis with a 65 Gy SIB took 4-yr locoregional RFS from 62% to 85% (HR 0·45) and pelvic nodal relapse from 29% to 8%, with **no** GI cost (7% vs 9% G2+). Toxicity tracked the prostate bed (OR 4·6 for G2+ GI), not the pelvic volume.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: ADT intensity was fixed at 6 months in both arms, so the difference is purely locoregional field size, yet ADT-free survival still improved to 77% vs 60% at 4 years (HR 0·60), with median time off ADT not reached under ENRT. For a systemic reader this argues for referral before escalating to an ARSI in EMBARK-eligible PSA-doubling-time patients.
